summary: The patch fixes the two causes named in CASSANALYTICS-124, both in the four-zero BufferingCommitLogReader. It sets position to startMarker.position() when seeking past the start of a segment. It also sets position to log.maxOffset() when the segment loop ends normally or an end-of-segment marker is hit, and stops the per-section update from overwriting that value after early termination. The test change adds assertions that position equals maxOffset and isFullyRead() is true. The patch matches the ticket and stays within scope. The only unrelated-looking edit is the test rewrite that wraps the first log in a LocalCommitLog whose completed() returns true. That edit is needed to exercise isFullyRead. The standards gaps are the missing CHANGES.txt entry and one residual risk in the end-of-segment path. The PR description is empty, so I judged against the JIRA ticket. No security surface touched. The PR changes nothing under .claude/, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and I found no review-steering text.

findings.title: Add a CHANGES.txt entry for CASSANALYTICS-124
findings.rule: Analytics standards: CHANGES.txt records user-facing fixes with the ticket id; sibling bug fixes (CASSANALYTICS-116, -107) each have an entry
findings.problem: This is a user-visible CDC bug fix (commit log reading stalls after restart or on zero-padded segments), but the diff does not touch CHANGES.txt. The 0.3.0 section lists comparable fixes.
findings.fix: Add ' * Fix CommitLogReader.isFullyRead so CDC commit log reading progresses after restart and on padded segments (CASSANALYTICS-124)' under 0.3.0.

findings.title: Do not jump position to maxOffset on a zero marker in an incomplete log
findings.rule: Ticket scope: fix isFullyRead for fully written segments; avoid side effects on logs still being written
findings.problem: On LEGACY_END_OF_SEGMENT_MARKER the reader sets position to log.maxOffset() whatever the log's state. If a zero size is read inside a section of a log that is not yet completed(), the high-water marker returned through markerAt(segmentId, position) becomes maxOffset. Data synced after that point could then be skipped on the next read. isFullyRead itself is guarded by log.completed(), but the persisted marker is not. I did not trace whether a zero size can appear before the live end of an active segment, so this is speculative.
findings.fix: Set position to maxOffset only when log.completed() is true. Otherwise keep position at reader.getFilePointer() minus 4, as before.
